paragraphs.text: See Isa 13:1.
paragraphs.anchor: The burden of Egypt.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Riding - sc., as a judge, or general of an army.
paragraphs.anchor: Behold the Lord rideth.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Speedily, suddenly, and irresistibly. Clouds are rarely seen in Egypt, where it raineth not; but in Eze 30:18 we read of a cloud that should cover Egypt. By "swift cloud" here some understand the Virgin Mary; others our Saviour’s body, or human nature. And they further tell us, that as soon as the child Jesus was brought into Egypt, down fell all the idols there, as Dagon did before the ark. {a} This they ground upon the following words: -
paragraphs.anchor: Upon a swift cloud

paragraphs.text: Whereby I conceive is only meant that their gods should not be able to help them, and should therefore lose their authority, be discredited and decried.
paragraphs.anchor: And the idols of Egypt shall be moved at his presence.

paragraphs.text: As it did, first when Sennacherib, and then when Nebuchadnezzar came against it.
paragraphs.anchor: And the heart of Egypt shall melt.

paragraphs.text: {a} Hist. Scholast.

Commiscebo Egyptios inter se, I will embroil them in a civil war. This happened, saith Junius, under King Psammeticus, after the death of Sethon, about the end of Hezekiah’s reign, or the beginning of Manasseh’s, while Isaiah was yet alive. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: And I will set the Egyptians against the Egyptians.

paragraphs.text: Or, Rectory against rectory; for as here in the heptarchy, so there the land was divided into many provinces or jurisdictions, even sixty-six, saith Ortelius.
paragraphs.anchor: And kingdom against kingdom.

paragraphs.text: {a} Herod., lib. ii. Diod. Sic., lib. i.

Fail and falter; their wits shall not serve them, but be drained and emptied, as the Hebrew word here signifieth. By spirit, here understand their wisdom, learning, and sharpness, for the which they were famous among, and frequented by other nations. Moses was skilled in their learning. {Act 7:23} Pythagoras, Plato, Solon, Anaxagoras, and other philosophers got much by them. Mercurius Trismegist saith of Egypt, that it was the image of heaven, and the temple of the whole world. By spirit here, some understand their familiar spirits. {a} See Lev 19:31.
paragraphs.anchor: And the spirit of Egypt shall fail.

paragraphs.text: Whereof they had great store (so that they were derided by other idolaters), but their chief deity was Latona, saith Herodotus.
paragraphs.anchor: And they shall seek to the idols.

paragraphs.text: Who have their name in Hebrew from their low or slow speaking.
paragraphs.anchor: And to the charmers.

paragraphs.text: {a} Aug. De Civit. Dei, lib. viii. cap. 14.
Heb., Shut up - sc., as fishes in a pond.
paragraphs.anchor: And the Egyptians will I give over.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Lords - viz., those twelve tyrants that reigned after Sethon, and were put down by Psammeticus, one of their own number, who afterwards reigned alone and with rigour. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: Into the hand of a cruel lord.

paragraphs.text: viz., Psammeticus, the father of that Pharaohnecho who slew Josiah. {2Ki 23:29} This fierce king reigned fifty-four years, and by his harshness caused 200,000 of his men of war to leave him, and to go into Ethiopia.
paragraphs.anchor: And a fierce king

paragraphs.text: {a} Herodot.

i.e., Their sea traffic shall be taken from them, to their very great loss. Historians testify, that by frequent navigation out of the Bay of Arabia into India and Trogloditiae, the revenue of Egypt was so increased, that Auletes, the father of Cleopatra, received thence yearly twelve thousand and five hundred talents.
paragraphs.anchor: And the waters shall fail from the sea

paragraphs.text: i.e., The river Nile, which watereth Egypt and maketh it fruitful. See Deu 11:9-10 Eze 29:3; Eze 29:9.
paragraphs.anchor: And the river shall be wasted and dried up

paragraphs.text: “ Creditur Aegyptus caruisse iuvantibus arva
Imbribus, atque annis sicca fuisse novem. ”
- Ovid. Art., lib. i.

The Assyrians shall, or some of their own fond and vainglorious princes shall drain the river Nile at several passages and in several places, to the impairing of the river and the impeaching of the state. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: And they shall turn the rivers far away.

paragraphs.text: These were of great use there; for of flags they made their barks and boats, mats also, wheels, baskets, &c.; of reeds they made their sails, ropes, paper, and a kind of juice serving them for food, {b} &c. As therefore the palm tree is to the Indians a cornucopia, yielding many commodities, so are reeds and flags to the Egyptians.
paragraphs.anchor: The reeds and flags shall wither.

paragraphs.text: {a} Herodot., lib. ii.
{b} Plin., lib. xiii. cap. 11.

i.e., By the streams of Nile; for where this river arriveth not, is nothing but a whitish sand, bearing no grass but two little weeds called suhit and gazul, which, burnt to ashes, maketh the finest crystal glasses.
paragraphs.anchor: The paper reeds by the brooks

paragraphs.text: As far as Nile overflows is a black mould, so fruitful as they do but throw in the seed and have four rich harvests in less than four months.
paragraphs.anchor: And everything sown by the brooks.

paragraphs.text: Because their trade decayeth, or they take pains to no purpose. {Isa 19:10}
paragraphs.anchor: The fishers also shall mourn.

paragraphs.text: sc., For want of materials, such as were wont to be sown by the brooks {Isa 19:7 1Ki 10:28 Pro 7:16 Eze 27:7} (Plin., lib. ix. cap. 1).
paragraphs.anchor: They that work in fine flax shall be confounded

paragraphs.text: Or rather whiteworks {a} - that is, white garments made of the fine flax of Egypt. These were much worn by nobles. {Pro 7:16 Dan 7:9} Whence also in Hebrew they have their name. {1Ki 21:8 Neh 2:16 Ecc 10:17, &c.}
paragraphs.anchor: They that weave networks.

paragraphs.text: {a} úåãéí, Albi seu candidati.
Heb., In the foundations, as Psa 11:3. Purposes are the foundation of practices, but are oft disappointed.
paragraphs.anchor: And they shall be broken in the purposes thereof.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Ponds of fowl, stagna voluptaria (Tremellius), standing pools of desire. In Hebrew, the word used elsewhere for a pond or fish pool signifieth a blessing also. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: And ponds for fish.

paragraphs.text: {a} Berecha.

Otherwise they would never have so ill-advised their king so to drain the river, for his pleasure, to the public detriment. Zoan was an ancient city in Egypt. {Num 13:22} The Septuagint and Vulgate versions call it Tunis. Here it was that Moses did all his wonders. {Psa 78:12 Exo 7:8-9} Here Pharaoh’s princes "took counsel, but not of God; and covered with a covering, but not of his Spirit, that they might add sin to sin." {Isa 30:1}
paragraphs.anchor: Surely the princes of Zoan are fools.

paragraphs.text: Such as was that of Machiavel, {a} the Florentine secretary, who proposeth Caesar Borgia, notwithstanding all his villanies, as the only example for a prince to imitate.
paragraphs.anchor: The counsel of the wise counsellors is become brutish.

paragraphs.text: How can ye for shame say so of yourselves? Or quomodo dictatis Pharaoni? How can ye dictate or put such words as these into your king’s mouth? What gross flattery is this?
paragraphs.anchor: How say ye unto Pharaoh?

paragraphs.text: Or, A son of "wise ones; as if wisdom were proper to you, and hereditary. The Egyptians cracked much of their wisdom, yet more of their antiquity, as if they were long before other people, yea, before the moon - as the Arcadians also boasted - and that their philosophy was very ancient. {b}
paragraphs.anchor: I am the son of the wise.

paragraphs.text: {a} De Principe, p. 185.
{b} Herod. lib. ii. - προσεληναοι, Lucian. - Plato in Timaeo.

q.d., Vile latens virtus: if they have that wisdom they pretend to, let them predict thy calamities and help to prevent them. Mihi hominun prudentia similis videtur talparum labori non sine dexteritate sub terra fodientium, sed ad lumen solis caecutientium, {a} The world’s wizards are like children, always standing on their heads and shaking their heels against heaven.
paragraphs.anchor: Where are they? where are thy wise men?

paragraphs.text: {a} Gasp. Ens.
Wilful fools; this they are told twice over, because hardly persuaded to it. See Isa 19:11.
paragraphs.anchor: The princes of Zoan are become fools.

paragraphs.text: Called also Moph, {Hos 9:6} and therehence Memphis, now Grand Cairo, famous once for the pyramids and monuments of the Egyptian kings.
paragraphs.anchor: The princes of Noph.

paragraphs.text: Heb., The corners {a} of the tribes or rectories - that is, either the king and chieftains, as some sense it; or, as others, all the inhabitants of the country, from one corner thereof unto another. How these wise men of Egypt deceived others is not expressed; but probably they did it by approving and cherishing the superstition, impiety, and carnal security of the princes and people.
paragraphs.anchor: Even they that are the stay of the tribes thereof.

paragraphs.text: {a} The free states of Switzerland are called cantons - i.e., corners.
Or, Given them to drink a spirit of giddiness. Heb., A spirit of extreme perversities; he hath stupified, and as it were intoxicated them with the "efficacy of error."
paragraphs.anchor: The Lord hath mingled a perverse spirit.

paragraphs.text: Psammeticus their king was twenty-eight years in besieging Azotus ere he could take it; and other things went on with them accordingly. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: And they have caused Egypt to err in every work.

paragraphs.text: {a} Herod., Euterp.
See on Isa 19:14.
paragraphs.anchor: Neither shall there be any work.

paragraphs.text: Feeble and faint-hearted, nihil mascule aut fortiter facturi, sed mulieribus meticulosiores. See Pro 28:1. {See Trapp on "Pro 28:1"}
paragraphs.anchor: In that day shall Egypt be like unto women.

paragraphs.text: When as yet he threateneth only; how much more when he striketh in good earnest? See Isa 30:32.
paragraphs.anchor: Because of the shaking of the hand of the Lord.

paragraphs.text: For how should Egypt hope to speed better than Judea had done? How Sethon, King of Egypt, was put to his trumps, as we say, when Sennacherib invaded Egypt, imploring the aid of his god Vulcan, whose priest he was, see Herodotus, lib. ii.
paragraphs.anchor: And the land of Judah shall be a terror unto Egypt.

paragraphs.text: When the gospel shall be there preached, whether by Mark the evangelist or others, as Clement, Origen, Didymus.
paragraphs.anchor: In that day.

paragraphs.text: A considerable number of Egyptians.
paragraphs.anchor: Five cities.

paragraphs.text: Called the Jews’ language, {Isa 36:11; Isa 36:13} the Hebrew tongue, wherein were written the lively oracles of God. This language, therefore, the elect Egyptians shall learn, and labour for that "pure lip," {Zep 3:9} to "speak as the oracles of God"; {1Pe 4:11} "wholesome words"; {2Ti 1:13} "right words"; {Job 6:25} "words of wisdom"; {Pro 1:6} "of truth and soberness"; {Act 26:25} to be examples to others, not only in faith and conversation, but also "in words and communication." {1Ti 4:12}
paragraphs.anchor: Speak the language of Canaan.

paragraphs.text: Devote themselves to his fear and service, taking a corporal oath for that purpose as in baptism, {a} and other holy covenants, whereupon haply they might be enabled to speak with tongues, the holy tongue especially, as most necessary for Christians. Here then we have a description of a true Christian, not such as the Jesuits in their catechism give us, viz., A Christian is he who believeth whatsoever the church of Rome commandeth to be believed, swearing fealty to her.
paragraphs.anchor: And swear to the Lord of hosts.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Nevertheless there shall be a few cities that shall despise Christian religion; and shall therefore be destroyed for neglecting so great salvation. It shall be easier for Sodom one day than for such. Others render the text Heliopolis, or the city of the sun, shall be accounted one, sc., of those five converted cities, and become consecrated to the Sun of righteousness. {b}
paragraphs.anchor: One shall be called the city of destruction

paragraphs.text: {a} Nempe susceptione baptismi. - Piscat.
{b} Joseph. Ant., lib. xiii. cap. 6.

A spiritual altar for spiritual sacrifices. {as Isa 19:20 Heb 13:10} Onias, the Jewish priest, who hereupon went and built an altar at Heliopolis in Egypt, and sacrificed to God there, was as much mistaken as the Anabaptists of Germany were in their Munster, which they termed New Jerusalem, and acted accordingly, sending forth apostles, casting out orthodox ministers, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: In that day shall there be an altar to the Lord.

paragraphs.text: That is, saith one, the gospels and writings of the apostles, that pillar and ground of truth, or a public confession of the Christian, faith. {Rom 10:9} An allusion to Jos 22:10; Jos 22:25. See Zec 14:9; Zec 14:20-21.
paragraphs.anchor: And a pillar in the border thereof.

paragraphs.text: The doctrine of Christ’s death is a clear testimony of God’s great love and kindness to mankind. {Rom 5:8}
paragraphs.anchor: And it shall be for a sign and for a witness.

paragraphs.text: As the Israelites sometimes had done under the Egyptian servitude. {Exo 3:9}
paragraphs.anchor: For they shall cry unto the Lord for their oppressors.

paragraphs.text: Not Moses but Messias, that great Saviour; {a} for God had laid his people’s "help on one that is mighty." {Psa 89:19} See Tit 2:13.
paragraphs.anchor: And he shall send them a Saviour.

paragraphs.text: {a} Servatorem et magnatem, vel magistrum.
They shall both know the Lord Christ, and be known of him. {as Gal 4:9} See Rom 10:20.
paragraphs.anchor: And the Lord shall be known to Egypt.

paragraphs.text: Perform "reasonable service," {Rom 12:1} such as whereof they can render a reason. Not a Samaritan service, {Joh 4:22} or Athenian {Act 17:23} - "Whom therefore ye ignorantly worship," &c. God will have no such blind sacrifices. {Mal 1:8}
paragraphs.anchor: And shall do sacrifce and oblation.

paragraphs.text: That in baptism especially.
paragraphs.anchor: Yea, they shall vow a vow, &c.

paragraphs.text: That he may bring it into the bond of the covenant. {Eze 20:37 Heb 12:9 Hos 6:1}
paragraphs.anchor: And the Lord shall smite Egypt.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Smiting and healing. Una eademque manus, &c. Una gerit bellum monstrat manus altera pacem; as it was said of Charles V. Facit opus alienum ut faciat proprium {Isa 28:20}
paragraphs.anchor: He shall smite and heal it.

paragraphs.text: Pardon their sins, heal their natures, and make up all breaches in their outward estates.
paragraphs.anchor: And shall heal them.

paragraphs.text: All hostility shall cease, and a blessed unanimity be settled among Christ’s subjects of several nations; hereunto way was made by the Roman empire, reducing both these great countries into provinces.
paragraphs.anchor: In that day there shall be an highway, &c.

paragraphs.text: Serve the Lord "with one shoulder." {as Zep 3:9}
paragraphs.anchor: And the Egyptians shall serve.

paragraphs.text: The posterity of Shem, Ham, and Japheth, shall concur in the communion of saints; the pale and partition wall being taken away.
paragraphs.anchor: In that day shall Israel be the third with Egypt.

paragraphs.text: The saints are so. Absque stationibus non staret mundus. If it were not for them, the world would soon shatter and fall in pieces.
paragraphs.anchor: Even a blessiing in the midst of the earth.

paragraphs.text: Or, For the Lord of hosts shall bless, and then he shall be blessed, {a} as Isaac said of Jacob. {Gen 27:33}
paragraphs.anchor: Whom the Lord af hosts shall bless.

paragraphs.text: A new title to Egypt, and no less honourable. Vide quantum profecerit Egyptus flagellis, saith Oecolampadius, here, i.e., see how Egypt hath got by her sufferings. See Isa 19:22. She who was not a people, but a rabble of rebels conspiring against heaven, is now owned and taken into covenant.
paragraphs.anchor: Blessed be Egypt, my people.

paragraphs.text: "For we are his workmanship created in Christ Jesus unto good works." {Eph 2:10}
paragraphs.anchor: And Assyria, the work of my hands.

paragraphs.text: This is, upon the matter, one and the same with the former; every regenerate person, whether Jew or Gentile, is all these three in conjunction. Oh the μυρωμακαριοτης, the heaped up happiness of all such! "Let Israel rejoice in him that made him; let the children of Zion be joyful in their king." {Psa 149:2} "For the Lord her God in the midst of her is mighty; he will save, he will rejoice over her with joy; he will rest in his love, he will joy over her with singing." {Zep 3:17}
paragraphs.anchor: And Israel mine inheritance.

paragraphs.text: {a} Jun.
